title: Russell Procope and joining John Kirby's band in 1944
summary: Charlie Shavers recommends Budd to replace Buster Bailey with Kirby in Baltimore, where he plays the seventh chair on tenor without music.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: I want to ask you this -- about Russell Procope, another New Yorker.

Russell Procope has always been one of the strongest and one of the best readers, saxophone players that I ever met. My first close, close experience was -- with him was when I joined the John Kirby band. I became the seventh man in the John Kirby band, and that was because Buster Bailey and Kirby had had an argument. So Charlie Shavers had heard me play Jelly, Jelly on clarinet -- on the record with Earl Hines, and he says, well, man, you better call Budd Johnson. So Charler Shavers and Kirby called me to come down and replace Buster Bailey. They were in Baltimore, Maryland, at the time, and this must have been early '44, 1944.

Well, I said, okay. So I had the presence of mind to take my tenor with me also, and then on my way down on the train, I got to thinking, I said, I must be out of my mind to think I'm going to take a clarinet and follow Buster Bailey in the John Kirby band.
And no way I can play that music, you know. But I'm game enough. I'm going to give it a try, but I know it's

impossible, and to my good fortune, when I got into Baltimore, Maryland, they were working at a cabaret there, and they had made up. So Kirby, being the nice man that he was, he said, look, you're here now, so you might as well stay. So they put me to work in the band as the seventh man, and I played tenor.

Now I didn't have any music, and I'm up there trying to fake a fourth part to the Kirby band. Can you imagine that? All of the music they were playing -- and in the meantime Charlie Shavers and myself was taking the parts and deciphering them and trying to make a fourth part, --
-- so I would have some music to play.
